source_ref: CC0 Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/DIU6BU (Bateman et al., STOPTHEBURN trial), single file 'STOPTHEBURN Data.xlsx' -- a REDCap export whose 'Survey Data' sheet carries the administered item wording as column headers (cols 20-56) and the administered option labels as cell values. Protocol paper: Bateman et al. 2020, 'Death Cafes for prevention of burnout in intensive care unit employees: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial (STOPTHEBURN)', Trials 21:1019, doi:10.1186/s13063-020-04929-4, CC BY 4.0 (PMC7729694) -- names the three instruments, gives the 2-week reference period for PHQ-8/GAD-7, gives the four survey timepoints, and gives the MBI subscale cut-scores used above to fix the subscale sizes. Rights source for the MBI: Mind Garden's own permissions page, which requires a purchased License to Administer and states that 'Only three sample items from this instrument may be included in your thesis or dissertation, and any other use must receive prior written permission from Mind Garden', plus a per-page copyright notice requirement.
note: PARTIAL SHIP ON RIGHTS GROUNDS: 15 of 37 items carry item_text, 22 do not. The split is exactly by instrument and it is visible in the data before any document is read, because the two blocks use different response ranges -- the 15 PHQ-8/GAD-7 items run 0-3 and the 22 MBI items run 0-6. WHY THE 22 ARE WITHHELD: the MBI-HSS is commercially published by Mind Garden and the restriction is quotable on both of Ben's block criteria at once -- a purchased License to Administer is required (a fee), and 'any other use must receive prior written permission from Mind Garden' (an explicit permission-required clause). Under Ben's 2026-09-06 ruling ('let's err on the side of not having things. so do not host') the item wording is not hosted. Note this differs from the standing 'source cannot share' exclusion in SKILL.md: this source DID share -- the depositors published all 22 MBI items as CC0 column headers -- so the bar is IRW's own conservatism about republishing a licensed instrument, not a publisher's refusal to the study team. WHY THE MBI ANCHORS DO SHIP WHILE THE ITEMS DO NOT, AND HOW TO REVERSE THAT IN ONE STEP: option_text for the MBI block is the 7-point frequency scale (Never / A few times a year or less / Once a month or less / A few times a month / Once a week / A few times a week / Every day). It ships for three reasons -- it is the answer format rather than item content, it was published in Maslach & Jackson's original 1981 journal article and is restated in this study's own CC BY protocol, and without it the resp column for 22 of 37 items is uninterpretable, which is the one thing an itemtext table exists to prevent. This is a judgement call inside Ben's ruling rather than something the ruling settles, so it is isolated for easy reversal: blanking option_text on section_id gilbert_meta_45_3 removes it and nothing else. ESCALATE TO BEN -- WITHHOLDING item_text HERE PROTECTS NOTHING. The live IRW item codes ARE the MBI item wording in snake_case: i_feel_burned_out_from_my_work, ive_become_more_callous_toward_people_since_i_took_this_job, i_dont_really_care_what_happens_to_some_patients, and 19 more. All 22 are already published verbatim in the gilbert_meta_45 RESPONSE table and are recoverable by anyone who reads a code, entirely independently of itemtext. The Prime Commandment requires all 37 codes to ship for the join to work, so the exposure cannot be closed from this side at all -- it would take a decision about the response table's item codes, which is outside this skill. The blank item_text column here should be read as IRW declining to ADD a hosted copy, not as the wording being unavailable. Same question likely applies to any other MBI table in the gilbert_meta family. REVERSE CODING (applies to interpreting resp, and it is not obvious from the codes): the 8 Personal Accomplishment items are reverse-coded in the live data relative to what respondents saw, so 'Never' maps to resp 6 and 'Every day' to resp 0 on those items, and high resp means more burnout uniformly across all 22 MBI items. This is not an assumption -- it is what makes the 851-cell reproduction close exactly, and the paper's own <33/48 cut-score independently fixes PA at 8 items. The recode happened upstream of this repo: there is no data/gilbert_meta_45 script, the table comes in through the gilbert_hte meta-analysis pipeline. correct_response is empty throughout: all three instruments are self-report frequency ratings with no key. section_prompt is empty because the REDCap export carries none. instructions is empty for the MBI block, since the MBI's own instruction paragraph is Mind Garden text and falls under the same withholding as the items.

ITEM TEXT IS WITHHELD FOR THE 22 MBI ITEMS. The MBI is commercially licensed by Mind Garden, which requires a purchased License to Administer and prior written permission for other uses, so IRW does not host the wording. The MBI response anchors are provided, since the resp column is otherwise uninterpretable. Higher resp means more burnout on all 22 MBI items, which is the opposite of the direction respondents answered in for those 8. Do not reverse them again. The mapping between each item's response options and its resp values is given per item in this table and reflects the reversal. The 'Not at all' anchor is spelled '(0-1 day)' on the PHQ-8 and '(0-1 days)' on the GAD-7; that difference is in the study's own survey forms and is transcribed as found. source_ref: CC BY 4.0 Mendeley Data doi:10.17632/bwkm69ycrc.1 (Bang, Li & Flynn, 'Evaluation of an Adaptive Game-Based Math Learning Program for Improving Early Elementary School Children's Math Knowledge'). Two files carry everything used: 'Student Assessment Items.docx', which reproduces all 38 items as 11 page images with the questions numbered 1-38, and 'Assessment_Master File_Shared.xlsx', whose 'Data Layout' sheet is the variable dictionary (learning objective and Common Core standard per item) and whose 'MM 2019 Spring Data' sheet holds the per-item scores and raw responses used for the reproduction and the derived key. Paper: Bang, Li & Flynn (2023), Early Childhood Education Journal 51(4), 717-732, doi:10.1007/s10643-022-01332-3.
note: ITEM TEXT IS A LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION FROM PAGE IMAGES, AND THE IMAGES ARE WHY THIS TOOK CARE. The deposit's item document is 11 JPEGs inside a .docx with no extractable text layer, so every stem and option was read off the images. Two deliberate limits on what got transcribed. First, NOTHING IRW WROTE IS IN item_text: where an item's stem refers to a picture ('How many birds are shown below?', 'Which picture represents twenty-three?') the words are transcribed and the picture is NOT described, per the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling. Where the response OPTIONS are pictures rather than text -- items 10, 11 and 23 -- no options are listed at all, so those three item_texts are stems only. Second, on-screen numeric material that is genuinely part of the item (count sequences, fact families, the lists of draggable numbers, the grid in item 6) IS transcribed, linearised into running text because a CSV cell cannot hold a grid. That linearisation is the one transformation applied and it is disclosed here rather than passed off as layout-faithful. OPTIONS LIVE IN item_text, NOT IN option_text, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The live resp is 0/1 -- an accuracy score, not an option index -- so a lettered option cannot be the 'response value assigned to a specific option_text'. Putting the options next to 0/1 would repeat the error corrected on kfcovid_Li2020 in batch_202. option_text is therefore empty throughout and the lettered options appear inside item_text, where they were displayed. correct_response carries the key in the standard's format (semicolons for multiple correct answers, as on item 13), with the option value in parentheses so the key is readable without re-reading the stem. KEY PROVENANCE: the key was NOT solved by IRW doing the arithmetic. It was derived from the deposit's own Wave1_<n>Response / Wave1_<n>Code column pairs, which reveal for every item exactly which response scores full credit, unambiguously (no response value ever scores both 0 and 1). key_source=derived_from_responses. IRW's only contribution is expressing six drag-and-drop keys in plain language instead of the platform's 'DEST_i-SRC_j' strings, which required establishing that SRC indexes the on-screen list row-major -- tested on all six, and arithmetically forced on four of them. SCORING QUIRK WORTH KNOWING: item 6 ('Count by 1s from the number 54') has six blanks and the deposit scores it 0-6, but the live table carries the dichotomised recode, so 6code = 1 only for all six blanks right. A 0 there means anything from zero to five blanks correct, which is a much lower bar than 0 on any other item. Its row coverage still follows the raw column, so 72 person-waves with a recode but no raw score are absent from the live table. RIGHTS -- SHIPPED, AND WHY THIS IS NOT THE MBI SITUATION IN gilbert_meta_45. The items were 'selected from Certica item bank', a commercial bank, but the depositors published all 38 in full under CC BY 4.0 and the document carries no copyright notice, no attribution requirement to Certica and no restriction of any kind. There is no quotable fee and no permission-required clause, which is Ben's block test, and SKILL.md's standing rule is explicit that a commercial instrument reproduced in full in an open-access deposit is extractable from that deposit. Contrast gilbert_meta_45, where Mind Garden's own terms are quotable on both counts. Flagging the adjacency so the two are not later remembered as having been treated inconsistently. The dictionary's Learning Objective column was used only as corroboration, not as text -- it reads as scoring metadata ('Student can recognize numerals up to 20'), not as anything a child read, and item 17's is blank in the deposit anyway.
public_note: Thirty-eight early-elementary mathematics items, administered at pre-test (wave 0) and post-test (wave 1). Items 1-31 were given at both; items 32-38 were added at post-test only, so they appear at wave 1 alone. Item text is transcribed verbatim from the study's own deposit, where the assessment is published as page images with the questions numbered 1-38 -- the same numbers the item codes carry. Several items depend on a picture (a collection to count, base-ten blocks, a hundred chart); for those, the wording is given and the picture is not described. Three items (10code, 11code, 23code) had picture response options rather than text ones, so their item_text is the stem alone. On-screen number sequences, fact families and lists of draggable numbers are included in item_text as running text. Response options appear inside item_text rather than in option_text, because resp here is a 0/1 correct/incorrect score rather than which option was chosen, so option_text is empty. correct_response gives the scoring key, taken from the deposit's own raw-response and score columns rather than worked out by IRW. ONE ITEM SCORES DIFFERENTLY FROM THE REST: 6code asks for six missing numbers in a counting sequence and is all-or-nothing in this table, so 1 means all six blanks correct and 0 means anything less. The deposit's own 0-6 partial-credit score for that item is not what this table carries. Verified by reproducing every one of the table's 138 item-by-response-by-wave cell counts exactly from the deposit, and by checking the shipped key for all 38 items against the key implied by the deposit's raw responses.

source_ref: CC0 Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/5OPIYU (Romero, Sandefur & Sandholtz, 'Partnership Schools for Liberia'), paper: American Economic Review 110(2), 364-400, doi:10.1257/aer.20181478. The deposit sits behind Dataverse Guestbook 80, which returns HTTP 400 to every API route, so the files were obtained by a human answering the guestbook form in a browser -- the same wall and the same workaround as batch_202's gilbert_meta_73. TWO KINDS OF FILE ARE USED AND THEY CHECK EACH OTHER: (1) the student-assessment Stata files inside 'PSL Baseline and Midline Dataverse Files.zip' -- rawdata_public/baseline/student/SA_CLEAN_Master_deidentified.dta and rawdata_public/midline/final/Student Assessment/PSL_SA_deidentified_cleaned.dta -- whose VARIABLE LABELS are the item wording; and (2) the printed instruments 'Baseline Survey Tools.zip' -> PSL_Baseline_Student_Assessment.pdf and 'Midline Survey Tools.zip' -> PSL_midline_student_assessment_final_printable.pdf, which supply the section structure, the child-facing enumerator script, the listening-comprehension story texts, and an explicit CORRECT ANSWER line per item.
note: PARTIAL SHIP: 25 of 37 codes carry item_text, 12 do not. THE CENTRAL FINDING, AND THE REASON FOR THE BLANKS: THE ITEM CODES ARE FORM POSITIONS, NOT ITEMS. The study fielded two different test forms -- baseline and midline -- and the live table pools them into wave 0 and wave 1 under ONE set of item codes. Of the codes defined on both forms, almost all carry DIFFERENT CONTENT at the two waves. Concretely, in gilbert_meta_14 addition_q2 is '6 + 1 = 7' at baseline and '0 + 3 =' at midline (which is baseline's addition_q3), and wordprob1 and wordprob2 are simply SWAPPED between the two forms; in gilbert_meta_13 objectid1 is a picture of a book at baseline and a mouse at midline, and reading_level1_comp1 is 'What does John do?' against a farming passage at baseline but 'Where did the wild cat run?' against an entirely different passage at midline. So there is no single item_text for those codes, and shipping either form's wording would be wrong for every row from the other wave. item_text is left blank for exactly those codes and populated for every code whose content is unambiguous -- the form-exclusive ones plus wordprob5, which is identical on both forms. This is a partial ship in the same sense as socialstereotype_hughes_2025_judgement and gilbert_meta_45, except the limit is a property of the response table rather than of the sources: the sources are complete and excellent. WORTH RAISING ON THE DATA SIDE. Pooling two forms' contents under one item code is the kind of thing that breaks the IRW `item` contract, and it is invisible to anyone reading the response table -- addition_q2 looks like one item. It is the same class of defect as the oxfordcovid_xue_2024 filter bug (#1996) and deserves its own issue rather than being buried in an itemtext note; a wave-specific code (or item_family) would fix it and would make ~2/3 of these two tables' item text shippable. A SECOND, SMALLER REASON FOR BLANK item_text, AND IT IS NOT THE SAME REASON. The objectid_ and numdiscrim_ codes are handbook stimuli: the child is shown a picture (objectid) or a pair of printed numbers (numdiscrim) and must name the object or say which number is bigger. For those the variable label is the EXPECTED ANSWER, not a question stem -- 'Chair', '425 (Four hundred twenty-five)'. Putting that in item_text would misrepresent an answer key as the wording a child read, so it ships as correct_response with item_text blank, per the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling, and the section_prompt carries the instrument's own spoken task ('Now here are some more images. I want you to point to each image and tell me what it is.' / 'Now I will show you some numbers. I will point to two numbers at a time and I want you to tell me which number is bigger.'). verify_psl_common.R test 3 distinguishes the two reasons explicitly so the blank counts reconcile. ON THE ARITHMETIC ITEMS' APPEARANCE: the instrument is enumerator-facing, so the baseline form prints the problem WITH its answer ('12 + 6 = 18') for the enumerator to mark against while the child works it in the student handbook. item_text is that string verbatim rather than a reconstructed '12 + 6 = ___', because the standard's rule is to transcribe literally and disclose, not to normalise silently; correct_response repeats the answer so it is usable without parsing the stem. The midline form prints the problem without the answer ('0 + 3 =') and states the key separately, which is one more sign the two forms are different documents. A PDF EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, HANDLED: the printed instruments render every lowercase 'w' followed by a spurious space, so extracted text reads 'w ordprob1', 'How  many', 'Show  me'. item_text is therefore taken from the .dta variable labels, which are clean, and the PDFs are used only for keys, sections and prompts. The de-artifacted PDF text still agrees with the labels on 49 of 49 (gilbert_meta_13) and 109 of 109 (gilbert_meta_14) item-form pairs, which is what establishes that the labels are administered wording rather than internal shorthand. The section_prompt strings were transcribed by hand with the artifact corrected; that correction is the only normalisation applied to any shipped text. option_text is empty throughout: resp is a 0/1 correct/incorrect score, not which option was chosen. The midline form also offered a '-88 Don't Know' code, which the deposit's own 07b_Student_Prep_Midline.do recodes to 0, so it is absent from the live resp set and correctly absent here. The listening-comprehension story texts ARE in the baseline instrument and ship as section_prompt. Note that midline listening_quest3-5 are word-for-word the same three questions as baseline listening_comp4-6 and carry the same three keys (Kakata; lions, elephants and snakes; they share their meat), so the hunter-and-son story is attached to that midline section too -- an inference, but a well-supported one. The midline Level-1 listening story (about Paul and football) is NOT printed in the midline form, so that section carries the listening instruction without a story.
public_note: 37 items from the reading and English test of the Partnership Schools for Liberia student assessment, administered at baseline (wave 0) and at the midline follow-up (wave 1). note: PARTIAL SHIP: 30 of 69 codes carry item_text, 39 do not. THE CENTRAL FINDING, AND THE REASON FOR THE BLANKS: THE ITEM CODES ARE FORM POSITIONS, NOT ITEMS. The study fielded two different test forms -- baseline and midline -- and the live table pools them into wave 0 and wave 1 under ONE set of item codes. Of the codes defined on both forms, almost all carry DIFFERENT CONTENT at the two waves. Concretely, in gilbert_meta_14 addition_q2 is '6 + 1 = 7' at baseline and '0 + 3 =' at midline (which is baseline's addition_q3), and wordprob1 and wordprob2 are simply SWAPPED between the two forms; in gilbert_meta_13 objectid1 is a picture of a book at baseline and a mouse at midline, and reading_level1_comp1 is 'What does John do?' against a farming passage at baseline but 'Where did the wild cat run?' against an entirely different passage at midline. So there is no single item_text for those codes, and shipping either form's wording would be wrong for every row from the other wave. item_text is left blank for exactly those codes and populated for every code whose content is unambiguous -- the form-exclusive ones plus wordprob5, which is identical on both forms. This is a partial ship in the same sense as socialstereotype_hughes_2025_judgement and gilbert_meta_45, except the limit is a property of the response table rather than of the sources: the sources are complete and excellent. WORTH RAISING ON THE DATA SIDE. Pooling two forms' contents under one item code is the kind of thing that breaks the IRW `item` contract, and it is invisible to anyone reading the response table -- addition_q2 looks like one item. It is the same class of defect as the oxfordcovid_xue_2024 filter bug (#1996) and deserves its own issue rather than being buried in an itemtext note; a wave-specific code (or item_family) would fix it and would make ~2/3 of these two tables' item text shippable. A SECOND, SMALLER REASON FOR BLANK item_text, AND IT IS NOT THE SAME REASON. The objectid_ and numdiscrim_ codes are handbook stimuli: the child is shown a picture (objectid) or a pair of printed numbers (numdiscrim) and must name the object or say which number is bigger. For those the variable label is the EXPECTED ANSWER, not a question stem -- 'Chair', '425 (Four hundred twenty-five)'. Putting that in item_text would misrepresent an answer key as the wording a child read, so it ships as correct_response with item_text blank, per the 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling, and the section_prompt carries the instrument's own spoken task ('Now here are some more images. I want you to point to each image and tell me what it is.' / 'Now I will show you some numbers. I will point to two numbers at a time and I want you to tell me which number is bigger.'). verify_psl_common.R test 3 distinguishes the two reasons explicitly so the blank counts reconcile. ON THE ARITHMETIC ITEMS' APPEARANCE: the instrument is enumerator-facing, so the baseline form prints the problem WITH its answer ('12 + 6 = 18') for the enumerator to mark against while the child works it in the student handbook. item_text is that string verbatim rather than a reconstructed '12 + 6 = ___', because the standard's rule is to transcribe literally and disclose, not to normalise silently; correct_response repeats the answer so it is usable without parsing the stem. The midline form prints the problem without the answer ('0 + 3 =') and states the key separately, which is one more sign the two forms are different documents. A PDF EXTRACTION ARTIFACT, HANDLED: the printed instruments render every lowercase 'w' followed by a spurious space, so extracted text reads 'w ordprob1', 'How  many', 'Show  me'. item_text is therefore taken from the .dta variable labels, which are clean, and the PDFs are used only for keys, sections and prompts. The de-artifacted PDF text still agrees with the labels on 49 of 49 (gilbert_meta_13) and 109 of 109 (gilbert_meta_14) item-form pairs, which is what establishes that the labels are administered wording rather than internal shorthand. The section_prompt strings were transcribed by hand with the artifact corrected; that correction is the only normalisation applied to any shipped text. option_text is empty throughout: resp is a 0/1 correct/incorrect score, not which option was chosen. The midline form also offered a '-88 Don't Know' code, which the deposit's own 07b_Student_Prep_Midline.do recodes to 0, so it is absent from the live resp set and correctly absent here. shape1-4 keys are the instrument's own 'CORRECT ANSWER = IMAGE n' references to numbered pictures in the student handbook, shipped verbatim; the handbook is not in the deposit, so the image identity is not recoverable, but the spoken stem ('Show me the circle') is the whole item. more_addition and more_multiplication are the only two midline-only math items with a printed stem rather than a bare expression, and their keys come from the form's '[Correct answer: n]' notes.

note: ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK, NOT A LITERAL ITEM, AND THAT IS INHERENT TO THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN A GAP. This is an ASER-family oral assessment: the printed tool shows a POOL of stimuli and instructs the enumerator to pick from it at random -- the baseline math sheet reads, in Hindi, 'ask them to read the digits below in order, then ask any 5 digits', and the two-digit identification task lists ten numbers of which any five are asked. So no fixed wording is a property of an item code, exactly as in gilbert_meta_70/71 in this same batch, and the honest text is the task. WHERE THE TEXT COMES FROM: the deposit's own variable labels in ml_merged.dta, verbatim except for stripping the leading question number ('q31 No. of 1to9 numbers Read' -> 'No. of 1to9 numbers Read'). The deposit's spelling is kept as found, including its 'substraction'. Nothing here is IRW prose. THE BASELINE LABELS ARE USED, NOT THE ENDLINE ONES, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE WITH A PROOF BEHIND IT. The endline label set is shifted by one position: e_caser_math_add2 reads 'q39 single digit subtraction' and e_caser_math_subtr1 reads only 'Q39', leaving q38 unused and q39 duplicated. The administration cascade settles which is right -- add2 is given only to children who PASSED add1 (n matches add1's passers exactly at both waves), which a subtraction item would not be -- so the variable NAMES are correct and those two endline labels are a deposit typo. The baseline labels q36-q39 have no gaps or repeats and describe the same five arithmetic tasks the printed endline tool shows, so they are the text shipped for all nine both-wave codes; subtr3 is endline-only and takes its own endline label. WHY THE ITEM TEXT IS THE SAME AT BOTH WAVES HERE, UNLIKE THE PSL TABLES: the two forms differ only in the specific numerals printed on the sheet (baseline single-digit addition shows 5+4 and 9+4, endline shows 4+3 and 8+3), not in the task. Since item_text is the task, one value is correct for both waves. resp IS AN ALL-CORRECT INDICATOR, NOT A RAW SCORE, and that is not visible from the response table. The deposit scores the reading and identification items as COUNTS (digits 1-9 read out of 9; 11-20 read out of 10; five numbers identified in each of three ranges) and the arithmetic items as Yes/No/No-response. The live 0/1 is 1 only for a perfect count or a Yes. Reproduced on nine of ten items to within the ~6% analysis-sample restriction. correct_response is therefore empty: there is no single key, because the enumerator selects the stimuli, and resp already encodes accuracy. option_text is empty for the same reason. DEFECT TO REPORT ON THE DATA SIDE -- caser_math_read1. Its live resp corresponds to raw code 9, which is eight of nine digits read, not raw code 10, which is all nine; the pass rate is 1.3% where the correct dichotomisation gives 58-64%. read1 is also the only code carried for all 14,576 participants at both waves instead of the ~94% analysis sample, so its missing values appear to have been filled with 0. Both are upstream of this repo. Item text is unaffected and ships; the resp needs its own issue, as with oxfordcovid_xue_2024 (#1996). Anyone using read1 as-is will read a near-floor item that is not one. section_prompt carries the two task groups the printed tool uses (number reading and identification, then arithmetic); the tool's spoken instructions are printed in Devanagari in a legacy font that does not extract, and translating them myself would put IRW prose in a field defined as administered wording, so they are not shipped.
public_note: Ten numeracy items from the child ASER test used in a maternal-literacy evaluation in Bihar, administered at baseline (wave 0) and endline (wave 1). caser_math_subtr3, two-digit carry-over subtraction, was added at endline and appears at wave 1 only. ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK, NOT A FIXED QUESTION. This is an orally administered ASER-style test: the printed sheet shows a pool of numbers and problems and the enumerator picks from it -- 'ask any 5 digits' -- so no single wording belongs to an item code. The text given is the study's own description of each task, taken verbatim from its data files. The baseline and endline sheets print different numerals for the same tasks, so one description is correct for both waves. TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE MODELLING THIS TABLE. First, resp is an ALL-CORRECT indicator, not a raw score: the study scored the reading and identification items as counts (nine digits, ten numbers, five numbers in each range) and this table gives 1 only for a perfect count. Second, it is a CASCADING test -- a child attempted two-digit addition only after passing one-digit addition, and two-digit subtraction only after passing one-digit subtraction -- so the harder items have far fewer responses and their pass rates are conditional on an already-selected, more able group. Comparing raw item means across levels will mislead. KNOWN PROBLEM WITH ONE ITEM: caser_math_read1 (reading digits 1-9) appears to be dichotomised one step too low, giving a 1.3% pass rate where the study's own coding implies 58-64%, and it is the only item recorded for every participant at both waves rather than the analysis sample. Its item text is correct; treat its resp as unreliable pending a data fix. Verified by the study's own variable labels, by subtr3 appearing at exactly the wave its code list defines, and by the cascade: each follow-on item's respondent count equals its gate item's number of passers exactly at both waves.
